ai.title: Revert auth refactor: restore checkAuthToken
ai.summary: Reverts the switch to getUserInfoFromApiKey, restoring checkAuthToken in backend/src/util/check-auth.ts and packages/internal/src/utils/auth.ts. Callers in usage.ts, middleware.ts, and publish/route.ts updated to use structured AuthResult. checkAdmin and WebSocketMiddleware execute signatures adjusted.

eli5.text: The system stopped using one login-checking method and went back to its previous, more structured login-check method that returns clearer pass/fail results. The backend's main usage endpoint and the live chat connection layer now use this restored check, with WebSocket handling slightly reorganized so admin checks rely on the same shared login logic. This is internal housekeeping already live today, so you won't notice any change in how you log in or use the assistant.

ai.title: Replace checkAuthToken with getUserInfoFromApiKey
ai.summary: Internal auth refactor replaces legacy `checkAuthToken` with `getUserInfoFromApiKey` in `backend/src/util/check-auth.ts`, `backend/src/api/usage.ts`, `web/src/app/api/agents/publish/route.ts`, and `backend/src/websockets/middleware.ts`. Removes session-token DB joins in `packages/internal/src/utils/auth.ts` in favor of API-key lookups. Updates `packages/internal/src/knowledge.md` to drop deprecated auth utilities documentation. `checkAuth` signature changes to require `getUserInfoFromApiKey` dependency injection instead of `fingerprintId`.

eli5.text: When you use the product, the way it checks that you're allowed in has switched from looking up your login session to looking up your API key. You won't see a difference on screen, but behind the scenes the system now pulls your account info from your API key instead of joining your web login session to a database record. This only affects internal requests that already use an API key, so normal sign-in behavior is unchanged.

ai.title: Strip prompt param before AI SDK calls
ai.summary: Added `prompt: undefined` to `streamText`, `generateText`, and `generateObject` calls in `backend/src/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts`. This prevents the `prompt` field from spreading into the AI SDK request when `messages` are explicitly provided via `convertCbToModelMessages`. Scope limited to the Vercel AI SDK backend adapter. Ensures clean parameter passing for structured and streaming outputs.

eli5.text: When your request reaches our internal AI helper, the system used to accidentally pass along an old-style prompt field alongside the properly formatted conversation history. Now it explicitly drops that leftover prompt field before forwarding the request, so the AI only sees the organized message sequence it expects. This affects how structured and streaming responses are assembled behind the scenes and is live today for all internal calls to that helper.

ai.title: Fix promptWithAgent logic in git-evals
ai.summary: Corrected inverted boolean logic for `promptWithAgent` in `runSingleEval` within `evals/git-evals/run-git-evals.ts`. The condition previously evaluated truthiness directly; it now negates the flag to determine if the spec serves as the sole prompt. This ensures the fallback decision object triggers only when prompting is disabled.

eli5.text: When the system runs a single test of the assistant's behavior, it now correctly checks whether the assistant is allowed to be prompted, instead of accidentally doing the opposite. If you were watching these background tests, you'd see that the fallback message saying 'Using spec as sole prompt' now appears only when prompting is actually turned off, rather than when it's turned on. This is a small behind-the-scenes fix to one internal test file, so most people won't notice any difference in daily use.
